key_idea: Tiling counts of a 2-row strip with parked cars are just products of Fibonacci numbers (free 2xk blocks separated by a vertical car), so split the 200 columns into two halves and meet in the middle on random block partitions.
sketch: A free 2xk block contributes F(k+1) and a single vertical car separates blocks, so a layout is a multiset of block widths with sum(k+1)<=200. Generate ~2M random partitions of a 100-column budget, store product mod p -> seed in a sorted table, then draw random right halves R and look up n*inv(prod(R)); expected about a thousand tries, ~0.6-1.2s total. n=0 is special: '##.' over '.##' leaves an isolated cell. Pitfall hit while solving: blocks must be drawn from a wide size range (3..40 columns) - with only small widths the set of reachable products is far smaller than 1e9+7 and the search never terminates. Multiple answers are valid so the sample checker cannot judge; outputs were validated for 130 values of n (including 0,1,10,27,p-1) with an independent profile-DP tiling counter that also checks the '#' cells form cars and length<=200.
